claims.explanation: Rivaroxaban is a factor Xa (F10) inhibitor, and its antiproliferative selectivity in this screen most plausibly reflects dependence on coagulation-factor/F10 signaling or on the PAR-mediated thrombin/FXa axis in certain tumor lineages, rather than a canonical anticoagulant effect. The pattern is not explained by a single common driver mutation; instead, sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/BRAF-pathway and TP53 alterations in colorectal, lung, and melanoma backgrounds, while many resistant lines carry PIK3CA/PTEN or receptor-tyrosine-kinase alterations, suggesting that MAPK-driven, F10/PAR-competent tumors are more vulnerable.
